blurb.en: Four small functions that do nothing but count their own steps, so the shape of a loop turns into a number you can compare.
blurb.zh: 四个小函数什么都不干，只数自己走了几步——循环的形状于是变成一个可以拿来比较的数字。

en: Complexity is about how the amount of work grows as the input gets bigger. Rather than timing anything - times change from one computer to the next, and even from one run to the next - each function here adds one to steps every time its innermost line runs. That count comes out the same on every machine, which is why this whole page counts steps instead of timing them.

The four shapes, for n = 100. One loop over range(n) runs n times: 100 steps. A loop inside a loop, both over range(n), runs n times n: 10000 steps. When the inner loop only visits the positions after i, it sees each pair (i, j) with i before j once, which is n(n-1)/2 steps: 4950, a little under half of n squared. A loop that halves n until nothing is left runs 7 times (100, 50, 25, 12, 6, 3, 1).

Big O keeps only the fastest-growing part and ignores constant factors. n(n-1)/2 is n squared over 2 minus n over 2; dropping the half and the smaller term leaves O(n^2), the same class as the full nested loop even though it does half the work. The halving loop is O(log n): it runs once for every binary digit of n - 5 times for n = 16, 7 times for n = 100.

The small rows are a warning: for n = 1 the single loop, the nested loop and the halving loop all take one step, and the pairs loop takes none. Big O describes what happens as n gets large; for tiny inputs the order can come out any way at all.
zh: 复杂度讲的是：输入变大时，工作量怎样跟着长。这里不计时——时间在不同电脑上不同，同一台电脑跑两次也不同——而是让每个函数在最里层那一行每执行一次，就给 steps 加一。这个数在哪台机器上都一样，所以本页一律数步数，不计时间。
四种形状，n = 100 时：对 range(n) 的一层循环跑 n 次，100 步。两层都对 range(n) 的嵌套循环跑 n 乘 n 次，10000 步。里层只走 i 之后的位置时，每一对 (i, j)（i 在 j 前面）只见一次，共 n(n-1)/2 步：4950，比 n 平方的一半略少。每次把 n 对半分、直到分没了的循环跑 7 次（100、50、25、12、6、3、1）。
大 O 只留增长最快的那一项，也不管常数倍。n(n-1)/2 等于 n 平方的一半减 n 的一半；去掉一半、再去掉小的那项，剩下 O(n^2)——与完整的嵌套循环同一级，尽管只干了一半的活。对半分的循环是 O(log n)：n 有几个二进制位它就跑几次——n = 16 时 5 次，n = 100 时 7 次。
表里小的那几行是个提醒：n = 1 时，一层循环、嵌套循环、对半分循环都只走一步，数对的循环一步都不走。大 O 说的是 n 变大以后的事；输入很小时，谁快谁慢怎样都有可能。

lineNotes.en: The inner loop does not depend on i: every pass of the outer loop costs n steps.
lineNotes.zh: 里层循环与 i 无关：外层每转一次都要花 n 步。

lineNotes.en: Doubling n from row to row makes the growth easy to read off.
lineNotes.zh: 每一行 n 翻一倍，增长的样子一眼就能读出来。

blurb.en: No measuring at all: work out log n, n, n log n, n squared and 2 to the n for n = 1, 2, 4 up to 1024, and watch them drift apart.
blurb.zh: 完全不测量：对 n = 1、2、4 一直到 1024，算出 log n、n、n log n、n 平方与 2 的 n 次方，看它们怎样越拉越开。

en: This table is the formula side of the page: pure arithmetic, nothing is run and counted. Each row doubles n. log n goes up by one per row, n doubles, n log n a little more than doubles, n squared goes up four times, and 2 to the n squares itself.

At n = 1024, log n is 10, n log n is 10240, n squared is 1048576 - about a million - and 2 to the 1024 has 309 digits. Already at n = 32 it is 4294967296, which is why the last column switches to a digit count once a number is longer than 8 digits. An O(2^n) method is hopeless beyond a few dozen items; a million steps for O(n^2) at n = 1024 is nothing to a computer; O(n log n) and O(n) hardly notice.

log n is worked out in whole numbers, without the math module. Every n in the table is a power of 2, and 2 to the k written in binary is a 1 followed by k zeros, k + 1 binary digits in all - so counting the digits of n and taking one away gives k exactly. In computing, log usually means log base 2, but for Big O the base does not matter: logs in different bases differ only by a constant factor.
The Doubling Experiment program on this page measures the same growth by running loops and dividing their step counts; this table predicts it from the formulas.
zh: 这张表是本页「公式」的那一面：纯算术，什么都不跑、什么都不数。每一行 n 翻一倍。log n 每行加一，n 翻倍，n log n 比翻倍多一点，n 平方变成四倍，2 的 n 次方则是自己乘自己。

n = 1024 时，log n 是 10，n log n 是 10240，n 平方是 1048576——约一百万——而 2 的 1024 次方有 309 位。n = 32 时它就已经是 4294967296 了，所以数字一超过 8 位，最后一列就改成只写「有几位」。O(2^n) 的方法过了几十个元素就没指望；O(n^2) 在 n = 1024 时一百万步，对电脑不算什么；O(n log n) 和 O(n) 几乎察觉不到。
log n 只用整数算，不用 math 模块。表里每个 n 都是 2 的整数次幂，而 2 的 k 次方写成二进制是一个 1 后面跟 k 个 0，一共 k + 1 位——所以数出 n 的二进制位数、再减一，就正好是 k。计算机里 log 一般指以 2 为底，但对大 O 来说底数无所谓：不同底数的对数只差一个常数倍。
本页的「倍增实验」真的跑循环、拿步数相除，量的是同一种增长；这张表是用公式预先算出来的。

lineNotes.en: Long numbers become a digit count, so every column stays narrow.
lineNotes.zh: 太长的数改写成位数，每一列都不会被撑宽。

lineNotes.en: k from 0 to 10 gives n = 1, 2, 4 up to 1024.

title.en: Counting Comparisons in Linear and Binary Search
title.zh: 数一数：线性查找与二分查找各比较几次

blurb.en: Both searches carry a counter. Looking for a value that is not there gives the worst case, and the two counts come out as n against about log2 n.
blurb.zh: 两种查找各带一个计数器。找一个根本不在表里的值是最坏情况，两边的次数分别是 n 与约 log2 n。

en: Instrumenting a function means adding a counter that records how often one chosen step happens, without changing what the function does. The step counted here is a comparison: one look at an item of the list. How the two searches work is on the Searching page; this program only counts.

The worst case is a target that is not in the list and is bigger than everything in it: linear search has to look at every item, and binary search keeps moving right until its range is empty. For a million items that is 1000000 looks against 20. For 10, 100, 1000 and 10000 items binary search needs 4, 7, 10 and 14 looks - the number of binary digits of n. Making the list ten times longer adds only three or four looks.

The demo then finds 700 in the numbers 0 to 999: linear search needs 701 looks and binary search 10. Even when it succeeds, binary search usually finds its target only after the range has shrunk to almost nothing, so its cost stays close to the worst case. Its last line checks that on every target at once: binary_found_total searches for each of the numbers 0 to 999 in turn, and the looks add up to 8987 - just under 9 per search, against 10 in the worst case.

Linear search is O(n) and binary search O(log n). The catch is that binary search needs a sorted list, and sorting costs more than a single linear search - binary search pays off when the same sorted list is searched many times.
zh: 给函数「插桩」，就是加一个计数器，记下某个选定的步骤发生了几次，而函数原本做的事一点不变。这里数的步骤是比较：看表里的一个元素一眼。两种查找本身怎么工作见「查找」一页；这个程序只负责数。
最坏情况是目标不在表里、而且比表里每个数都大：线性查找得把每个元素都看一遍，二分查找则一路往右收，直到区间为空。一百万个元素时是 1000000 次对 20 次。10、100、1000、10000 个元素时，二分查找分别要看 4、7、10、14 次——正是 n 的二进制位数。表长乘以十，只多看三四次。
演示接着在 0 到 999 里找 700：线性查找看了 701 次，二分查找 10 次。二分查找即使找得到，通常也要等区间缩到几乎没有时才碰上目标，所以花费仍然接近最坏情况。演示的最后一行把每个目标都试一遍：binary_found_total 依次查找 0 到 999 里的每一个数，一共看了 8987 次——每次不到 9 次，最坏情况是 10 次。
线性查找是 O(n)，二分查找是 O(log n)。代价是二分查找要求表已经排好序，而排序比一次线性查找贵——同一张有序表要反复查很多次时，二分查找才划算。

lineNotes.en: The count went up before this test, so a hit includes the look that found it.
lineNotes.zh: 计数在这次判断之前已经加过了，所以找到时，找到它的那一次也算在内。

lineNotes.en: A successful search, for comparison with the worst case above.
lineNotes.zh: 一次找得到的查找，拿来与上面的最坏情况对照。

blurb.en: Every shift fixes exactly one pair that is out of order, so the count equals the number of such pairs: none for a sorted list, n(n-1)/2 for a reversed one.
blurb.zh: 每右移一次，恰好理顺一对逆序的元素，所以右移次数就等于逆序对的个数：有序表是零，倒序表是 n(n-1)/2。

en: How insertion sort works is on the Sorting page. Here it carries a counter for its most frequent step: moving an item one place to the right to make room for key. It sorts a copy, so the list passed in is left exactly as it was.

Why the count means something: two positions i before j form an inversion when the item at i is bigger than the item at j. Each shift moves key past exactly one bigger item on its left, which removes exactly that one inversion and no other. So the number of shifts is exactly the number of inversions in the input - a property of the data, not of the code.

The demo: an already-sorted list needs 0 shifts at every size - the best case, O(n) in all, since each item is still compared once. A reversed list is the worst case, with every pair inverted: 45 shifts for 10 items, 4950 for 100 and 499500 for 1000, exactly n(n-1)/2, which is O(n^2). The scrambled list [(i * 7) % n for i in range(n)] lands in between: 18, 2163 and 213213.

Two equal items are not an inversion. That is why the shift test uses a strict comparison: shifting on equal items as well would make the count too high, and it would also swap equal items past each other, so the sort would no longer be stable.
zh: 插入排序怎么工作见「排序」一页。这里给它最常做的那一步配了一个计数器：把一个元素右移一格，给 key 腾位置。它排的是一份副本，传进来的表原样不动。
为什么这个数有意义：位置 i 在 j 前面、而 i 上的元素比 j 上的大，这两个位置就构成一个逆序对。每次右移都让 key 越过它左边恰好一个更大的元素，恰好消掉这一个逆序对、不多不少。所以右移次数就正好等于输入里的逆序对数——这是数据的性质，不是代码的性质。
演示：已排好序的表，不管多长都是 0 次右移——最好情况，总共 O(n)，因为每个元素仍要比较一次。倒序表是最坏情况，每一对都是逆序：10 个元素 45 次，100 个 4950 次，1000 个 499500 次，正好 n(n-1)/2，也就是 O(n^2)。打乱的表 [(i * 7) % n for i in range(n)] 落在两者之间：18、2163、213213。
两个相等的元素不算逆序。所以判断要不要右移用的是严格比较：若相等也右移，次数就会偏多，而且相等的元素会互相越过，排序也就不再稳定。

lineNotes.at: scrambled = [(i * 7) % n for i in range(n)]
lineNotes.en: n is 10, 100 or 1000, none of them a multiple of 7, so this is every number from 0 to n - 1 exactly once, in a fixed scrambled order - no random module needed.
lineNotes.zh: n 取 10、100、1000，都不是 7 的倍数，所以这张表恰好是 0 到 n - 1 每个数各一次、按一个固定的乱序排——用不着 random 模块。

lineNotes.en: key drops into the gap the shifts left behind.
lineNotes.zh: key 落进右移腾出来的空位。

title.en: Merge Sort against Insertion Sort, Counted
title.zh: 归并排序对插入排序：数比较次数

blurb.en: The same scrambled input goes to both sorts. For 8 items they are close; for 512 items insertion sort makes almost 18 times as many comparisons.
blurb.zh: 同一份打乱的输入交给两种排序。8 个元素时两者差不多；512 个元素时，插入排序的比较次数将近是归并排序的 18 倍。

en: Both sorts are explained on the Sorting page; here each one only counts comparisons between two items. insertion_comparisons counts every time an item is compared with key, including the comparison that ends the inner loop. merge_sort_count hands back the sorted list and its count together as a pair; each level adds the comparisons made by its own merge to the counts the two halves brought back. (How the recursion itself works is on the Recursion page.)

Results on the scrambled input [(i * 7) % n for i in range(n)]: for n = 8, insertion sort makes 28 comparisons and merge sort 14; for n = 32, 256 and 124; for n = 128, 3664 and 663; for n = 512, 57232 and 3224. The ratio grows from 2.0 to 2.1, 5.5 and 17.8.

That is O(n^2) against O(n log n): each time n is multiplied by four, insertion sort's count goes up roughly sixteen times and merge sort's only a little more than four times, so the gap keeps widening. (For n = 8 this input is almost exactly reversed, because 7 is one less than 8 - so at n = 8 insertion sort is at its worst, and merge sort still only halves the count.)

Insertion sort still has its place. On a list that is already sorted it makes only n - 1 comparisons, while merge sort makes about n log n whatever the input, and for very short lists insertion sort's simplicity wins. Real sorting libraries use insertion sort for short stretches for exactly this reason.
zh: 两种排序怎么工作见「排序」一页；这里各自只数「两个元素之间的比较」。insertion_comparisons 每拿一个元素与 key 比一次就记一次，连让里层循环停下的那一次也算。merge_sort_count 把排好的表和次数配成一对一起交回；每一层把自己合并时的比较次数，加到两半各自带回来的次数上。（递归本身的机制见「递归」一页。）
在打乱的输入 [(i * 7) % n for i in range(n)] 上：n = 8 时插入排序比较 28 次、归并排序 14 次；n = 32 时 256 次对 124 次；n = 128 时 3664 次对 663 次；n = 512 时 57232 次对 3224 次。倍数从 2.0 涨到 2.1、5.5、17.8。
这就是 O(n^2) 对 O(n log n)：n 每乘以四，插入排序的次数大约变成十六倍，归并排序只比四倍多一点，差距越拉越大。（n = 8 时这份输入几乎正好是倒序，因为 7 比 8 小一——所以 n = 8 时插入排序正处在最坏的情况，归并排序也只把次数减了一半。）
插入排序也有它的用处。表已经排好序时它只比较 n - 1 次，而归并排序不管输入如何都要约 n log n 次；很短的表上，插入排序简单反而占便宜。真正的排序库在短的片段上改用插入排序，正是这个原因。

lineNotes.en: Zero or one item is already sorted, and it took no comparisons to find that out.
lineNotes.zh: 零个或一个元素本来就是有序的，得出这一点一次比较都不用。

lineNotes.en: One comparison of left[i] with right[j] - the only place a merge compares anything.
lineNotes.zh: left[i] 与 right[j] 比一次——合并时只有这里在比较。

blurb.en: Double n five times and divide each step count by the one before: the ratio settles near 2 for O(n), near 4 for O(n^2), and a little above 2 for O(n log n).
blurb.zh: 把 n 连续翻倍五次，每次拿新步数除以上一次：O(n) 的倍数趋近 2，O(n^2) 趋近 4，O(n log n) 则比 2 多一点。

en: You do not have to read an algorithm to estimate its order: run it, double the size of the input, and see how many times more work it does. doubling_ratios takes the step-counting function itself as an argument - a function passed around like any other value - starts at n = 16 and doubles five times, up to 512.

largest counts the n - 1 comparisons needed to find the biggest of n items: its ratios are 2.07, 2.03, 2.02, 2.01 and 2.00. all pairs counts the n(n-1)/2 pairs: 4.13, 4.06, 4.03, 4.02 and 4.01. halving runs a halving loop once for every item, n times log2 n steps: 2.50, 2.40, 2.33, 2.29 and 2.25.

Reading the ratios: about 2 means doubling the input doubles the work - O(n). About 4 means it quadruples the work - O(n^2); about 8 would mean O(n^3). A little more than 2 and creeping down slowly is O(n log n): the log goes up by one each time n doubles, so the ratio is 2 times (k + 1) over k, which only approaches 2 as k grows.

The first ratios are furthest from their limits because of the smaller terms - the minus 1 in n - 1, the minus n over 2 in n(n-1)/2. As n grows those matter less and less, which is exactly why Big O leaves them out. Growth Rates Side by Side on this page predicts the same shapes from the formulas; this program measures them.
zh: 估一个算法的阶，不一定要读懂它：跑一跑，把输入翻一倍，看工作量变成几倍。doubling_ratios 把「数步数的函数」本身当作实参接进来——函数也能像别的值一样传来传去——从 n = 16 起，连续翻倍五次，到 512。
largest 数的是在 n 个元素里找最大值要比较的 n - 1 次：倍数依次是 2.07、2.03、2.02、2.01、2.00。all pairs 数 n(n-1)/2 对：4.13、4.06、4.03、4.02、4.01。halving 对每个元素各跑一遍对半分的循环，共 n 乘 log2 n 步：2.50、2.40、2.33、2.29、2.25。
怎么读这些倍数：约 2，说明输入翻倍、工作量也翻倍——O(n)。约 4，说明工作量变成四倍——O(n^2)；约 8 就是 O(n^3)。比 2 多一点、又慢慢往下降的，是 O(n log n)：n 每翻一倍，log 只加一，所以倍数是 2 乘以 (k + 1) / k，k 越大才越接近 2。
最前面几个倍数离极限最远，是那些小项在作怪——n - 1 里的减一，n(n-1)/2 里的减 n 的一半。n 越大它们越无足轻重，这正是大 O 把它们略去的理由。本页的「增长率并排看」用公式预言同样的形状；这个程序是把它们量出来。

lineNotes.en: One halving: the inner loop is the halving loop, run afresh for every item.
lineNotes.zh: 对半分一次：里层就是那个对半分的循环，每个元素都重新跑一遍。

lineNotes.en: The same experiment for each task: start at 16, double five times.
lineNotes.zh: 每个任务做同一个实验：从 16 起，翻倍五次。

title.zh: 有没有重复：每一对都比

blurb.en: Two loops compare each position with every later one: simple, needs nothing from the list, and O(n^2).
blurb.zh: 两层循环，把每个位置与它后面的每个位置都比一次：简单、对列表毫无要求，代价是 O(n^2)。

en: The outer loop picks a position i and the inner loop every position after it, so each pair is compared once and no item is compared with itself. The first equal pair settles the answer at once; the answer no can only be given after every pair has been compared, so that line sits after both loops.

The worst case is a list with no duplicates at all: n(n-1)/2 comparisons. For 1000 distinct items that is 499500; for 10000 items it is 49995000 - a hundred times the work for ten times the input. O(n^2) time, but no extra memory beyond two loop variables.

The same question is answered faster by Has Duplicates: Sort, Then Look Next Door and Has Duplicates: Remember in a Set on this page. The demo is the same for all three versions: [3, 1, 4, 1, 5] has 1 twice, [2, 7, 1, 8] has no repeat, the empty list has nothing to repeat, and strings work just as well as numbers.
zh: 外层循环选一个位置 i，里层循环走遍它后面的每个位置，所以每一对只比一次，也没有哪个元素跟自己比。第一对相等的一出现，答案立刻定了；「没有」这个答案却必须等每一对都比过才能给，所以那一行放在两层循环之后。
最坏情况是表里根本没有重复：要比 n(n-1)/2 次。1000 个互不相同的元素是 499500 次；10000 个是 49995000 次——输入变成十倍，工作量变成一百倍。时间 O(n^2)，但除了两个循环变量，不要任何额外内存。
本页的「有没有重复：先排序，再看邻居」与「有没有重复：用集合记住」回答同一个问题，都更快。三个版本的演示都一样：[3, 1, 4, 1, 5] 里 1 出现两次；[2, 7, 1, 8] 没有重复；空表里没有东西可以重复；字符串和数字一样能用。

lineNotes.en: One comparison - the step whose count makes this O(n^2).
lineNotes.zh: 一次比较——正是它的次数让这个版本成了 O(n^2)。

title.en: Has Duplicates: Sort, Then Look Next Door
title.zh: 有没有重复：先排序，再看邻居

blurb.en: Sort a copy, and any equal values end up side by side, so one pass comparing neighbours is enough: O(n log n).
blurb.zh: 把一份副本排好序，相等的值就一定挨在一起，于是只要走一遍、比一比相邻的两个：O(n log n)。

en: After sorting, equal values cannot be apart: anything sorted in between them would have to be equal to them as well. So instead of comparing every pair, compare each item with the one just before it - only n - 1 comparisons.

Sorting takes O(n log n) comparisons (the Sorting page shows where that comes from for merge sort) and the pass takes O(n), so the total is O(n log n). For 1000 items that is roughly ten thousand comparisons for the sort plus 999 for the pass, against 499500 for comparing every pair.

The copy matters. The built-in used here builds a new sorted list and leaves items alone, whereas calling .sort() on items would rearrange the caller's list as a side effect of a question that should only look. The convention to remember: list.sort() sorts in place and returns None; the built-in returns a new list.

Sorting needs the items to be comparable with each other: a list mixing numbers and strings cannot be sorted, so this version fails on it, while Has Duplicates: Remember in a Set only needs equality. The demo is the same for all three versions: [3, 1, 4, 1, 5] has 1 twice, [2, 7, 1, 8] has no repeat, the empty list has nothing to repeat, and strings work just as well as numbers.
zh: 排好序以后，相等的值不可能分开：排在它们中间的任何东西也必须和它们相等。所以不必每一对都比，只要把每个元素与它前面那一个比——只要 n - 1 次。
排序要 O(n log n) 次比较（归并排序为什么是这样见「排序」一页），走一遍是 O(n)，合起来 O(n log n)。1000 个元素时，排序约一万次、走一遍 999 次，对比每一对都比的 499500 次。
复制这一步很要紧。这里用的内置函数另建一张排好序的新表、不碰 items；而对 items 调 .sort() 会把调用方的表重新排列——一个本该只看不动的问题，却留下了副作用。要记住的约定：list.sort() 原地排序、返回 None；那个内置函数返回一张新表。
排序要求元素之间能比大小：数字和字符串混在一起的表排不了序，这个版本在它上面会出错；「有没有重复：用集合记住」只需要能判相等。三个版本的演示都一样：[3, 1, 4, 1, 5] 里 1 出现两次；[2, 7, 1, 8] 没有重复；空表里没有东西可以重复；字符串和数字一样能用。

lineNotes.en: Starts at 1, because position 0 has no left neighbour.
lineNotes.zh: 从 1 开始，因为位置 0 没有左邻。

title.en: Has Duplicates: Remember in a Set
title.zh: 有没有重复：用集合记住

blurb.en: Walk through once, keeping every value seen so far in a set. Checking a set takes about the same time however big it is, so the whole walk is O(n).
blurb.zh: 走一遍，把见过的每个值都记进集合。查集合花的时间与它多大几乎无关，所以整趟是 O(n)。

en: Each item is checked against the set of values seen before it. If it is already there, that is a duplicate; if not, it is remembered and the walk goes on. One pass: at most n checks and n additions.

The speed comes from hashing. A set does not compare the value with every member: it works out from the value itself where that value would be stored and looks only there, so in takes about the same time for a set of ten items as for a million. (How such a table is built is on the Searching page.) The same in on a list would compare with every item, and the whole method would slide back to O(n^2).

The price is memory: the set may end up holding all n values - O(n) extra space, where Has Duplicates: Compare Every Pair needed none. Trading space for time is the most common trade in algorithm design. For 1000 distinct items: 1000 set checks, against 499500 comparisons for every pair.

Items must be hashable - numbers, strings and tuples are, lists are not - but they need not be comparable by size. The demo is the same for all three versions: [3, 1, 4, 1, 5] has 1 twice, [2, 7, 1, 8] has no repeat, the empty list has nothing to repeat, and strings work just as well as numbers.
zh: 每个元素都拿去与「在它之前见过的值」组成的集合对照。已经在里面，就是重复；不在，就记下来接着走。只走一遍：至多 n 次查、n 次加。
快来自哈希。集合不会把这个值与每个成员逐个比：它从值本身算出这个值该存在哪儿，只去那儿看一眼，所以 in 查一个十个元素的集合和查一个一百万元素的集合，花的时间差不多。（这样的表是怎么建的见「查找」一页。）同样的 in 若用在列表上，就要与每个元素逐个比，整个方法又滑回 O(n^2)。
代价是内存：集合最后可能装下全部 n 个值——O(n) 的额外空间，而「有没有重复：每一对都比」一点都不用。拿空间换时间，是算法设计里最常见的交换。1000 个互不相同的元素：查 1000 次集合，对比每一对都比的 499500 次。
元素必须可哈希——数字、字符串、元组可以，列表不行——但不必能比大小。三个版本的演示都一样：[3, 1, 4, 1, 5] 里 1 出现两次；[2, 7, 1, 8] 没有重复；空表里没有东西可以重复；字符串和数字一样能用。

lineNotes.en: An empty set - {} would be an empty dictionary.
lineNotes.zh: 空集合——写成 {} 就成了空字典。

title.zh: 最大子段和：每个起点都试

blurb.en: For each starting position, grow the run to the right one item at a time and keep a running total: O(n^2), without adding anything up twice.
blurb.zh: 对每个起点，把这一段一次一个元素往右加长，同时维护一个累加的和：O(n^2)，而且没有哪一段要从头重加。

en: The problem: in a list of numbers, some positive and some negative, find the largest total of a run of neighbouring items - at least one item long. It is only defined for a list that is not empty.

The most obvious method tries every start and every end and adds up the items between them - three nested loops, O(n^3). This version keeps a running total instead: when end moves one place right, total only needs the new item added. Two loops over n(n+1)/2 runs, O(n^2): 45 runs for the nine-item example, 500500 for 1000 items.
Where best starts matters. For [-8, -3, -6, -2, -5, -4] the answer is -2: the best run is the single least negative item. Starting best at 0 would give 0, a total that no run adds up to.

Maximum Subarray: Divide and Conquer does it in O(n log n) and Maximum Subarray: One Pass (Kadane) in O(n). The demo is the same for all three versions: 6 for [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4] (the run 4, -1, 2, 1), -2 for the all-negative list, 5 for the single item 5, and 4 for [2, -1, 2, -1, 2], where the best run is the whole list.
zh: 问题：一张有正有负的数字表里，找出一段相邻元素（至少一个）的最大和。它只对非空的表有定义。
最直接的办法是每个起点、每个终点都试，把中间的元素加起来——三层循环，O(n^3)。这个版本改为维护一个累加的和：end 往右挪一格，total 只要加上新来的那一个。两层循环，共 n(n+1)/2 段，O(n^2)：九个元素的例子是 45 段，1000 个元素是 500500 段。
best 从哪儿起很要紧。[-8, -3, -6, -2, -5, -4] 的答案是 -2：最好的一段就是那个最不负的元素自己。best 若从 0 起，就会交回 0——没有哪一段加起来是 0。
「最大子段和：分而治之」用 O(n log n) 做到，「最大子段和：一遍扫描（Kadane）」用 O(n)。三个版本的演示都一样：[-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4] 得 6（那一段是 4, -1, 2, 1）；全是负数的表得 -2；只有一个元素 5 的表得 5；[2, -1, 2, -1, 2] 得 4，最好的一段就是整张表。

lineNotes.en: One new item added to the run from start to end - no re-adding from start.
lineNotes.zh: 给从 start 到 end 的这一段加上新来的一个元素——不必从 start 重新加起。

blurb.en: The best run lies in the left half, in the right half, or across the middle. The first two are the same problem on half the list; the third takes one pass.
blurb.zh: 最好的一段要么全在左半，要么全在右半，要么跨过中点。前两种是同一个问题换成半张表，第三种走一遍就够。

en: Divide and conquer splits a problem into smaller copies of itself. Cut the list in the middle: the best run is wholly in the left half, wholly in the right half, or it crosses the middle. The first two are the same question on a shorter list, so the function asks itself; the base case is a list of one item, whose only run is that item. (How recursion works is on the Recursion page.)

A run across the middle must take the item just left of the middle and the item just right of it, so its best total is the best reading leftwards from the middle plus the best reading rightwards. best_prefix gives the best total of a run that starts at the front of a list; turning the left half round makes its front the middle.

Cost: each level of splitting does O(n) work - the crossing sums, plus the slices, which copy - and halving gives about log2 n levels, so O(n log n) in all, the same pattern as merge sort. For 1000 items that is about 10 levels of about 1000 steps each, against the 500500 runs of Maximum Subarray: Every Start.

The demo is the same for all three versions: 6 for [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4] (the run 4, -1, 2, 1), -2 for the all-negative list, 5 for the single item 5, and 4 for [2, -1, 2, -1, 2], where the best run is the whole list. For [5] the base case answers straight away.
zh: 分而治之，是把一个问题拆成几个更小的「自己」。从中间切开：最好的一段要么全在左半，要么全在右半，要么跨过中点。前两种是同一个问题换成更短的表，所以函数去问它自己；基例是只有一个元素的表，它唯一的一段就是那个元素。（递归的机制见「递归」一页。）
跨过中点的一段，必须包含中点左边那一格和右边那一格，所以它的最好总和 = 从中点往左读能拿到的最大和 + 往右读能拿到的最大和。best_prefix 给出从表头开始的一段的最大和；把左半倒过来，它的表头就成了中点。
代价：每一层切分做 O(n) 的活——跨中点的求和，外加切片（切片会复制）——对半切约有 log2 n 层，合起来 O(n log n)，与归并排序同一个模式。1000 个元素时约 10 层、每层约 1000 步，对比「最大子段和：每个起点都试」的 500500 段。
三个版本的演示都一样：[-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4] 得 6（那一段是 4, -1, 2, 1）；全是负数的表得 -2；只有一个元素 5 的表得 5；[2, -1, 2, -1, 2] 得 4，最好的一段就是整张表。[5] 一进来就由基例直接回答。

lineNotes.en: Base case: one item, one run.
lineNotes.zh: 基例：一个元素，只有一段。

lineNotes.en: Best total of a run that starts at the front and ends here.
lineNotes.zh: 从表头开始、到这里结束的那一段的最大和。

blurb.en: Carry one number along: the best total of a run ending at the current item. Each step either extends that run or starts afresh - O(n).
blurb.zh: 一路只带着一个数：以当前元素结尾的那一段的最大和。每一步要么接着这一段，要么从头另起——O(n)。

en: current is the best total of a run that ends exactly at the item just reached. For the next item there are only two candidates: the item on its own, or the item added to the best run ending just before it. Taking the larger of the two is all the work each step does, and best keeps the largest current seen so far.

When current has gone negative, carrying it along would only drag the next item down, so the run starts again - that is what choosing the item on its own means. For [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4], current goes -2, 1, -2, 4, 3, 5, 6, 1, 5 and best ends at 6.

Both start from the first item, not from 0, so an all-negative list gives its least negative item: -2 for [-8, -3, -6, -2, -5, -4]. One pass of n - 1 steps, O(n) time and no extra memory: 999 steps for 1000 items, against the 500500 runs of Maximum Subarray: Every Start.

The demo is the same for all three versions: 6 for [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4] (the run 4, -1, 2, 1), -2 for the all-negative list, 5 for the single item 5, and 4 for [2, -1, 2, -1, 2], where the best run is the whole list.
zh: current 是「恰好以刚走到的这个元素结尾」的一段的最大和。对下一个元素，只有两个候选：它自己单独一段，或者它接在「以前一个元素结尾的最好一段」后面。两者取大，就是每一步全部的活；best 记住到目前为止见过的最大的 current。
current 一旦变成负数，带着它只会把下一个元素往下拖，所以就从头另起——「只取这个元素自己」说的就是这个。对 [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4]，current 依次是 -2、1、-2、4、3、5、6、1、5，best 最后是 6。
两者都从第一个元素起，而不是从 0 起，所以全是负数的表交回它最不负的那个元素：[-8, -3, -6, -2, -5, -4] 得 -2。只走一遍，n - 1 步，O(n) 时间、不要额外内存：1000 个元素 999 步，对比「最大子段和：每个起点都试」的 500500 段。
三个版本的演示都一样：[-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4] 得 6（那一段是 4, -1, 2, 1）；全是负数的表得 -2；只有一个元素 5 的表得 5；[2, -1, 2, -1, 2] 得 4，最好的一段就是整张表。

lineNotes.en: Both start as the first item: the only run that ends there is the item itself.
lineNotes.zh: 两个都从第一个元素起：以它结尾的只有它自己这一段。

lineNotes.en: The first item is already used, so the walk starts from the second.
lineNotes.zh: 第一个元素已经用过了，所以从第二个开始走。
